title: Dense Ranks for Every Value
statement:
You get an integer array arr. Replace every element with its rank:

  • the smallest value gets rank 1;
  • equal values get the same rank;
  • ranks have no gaps: the next larger distinct value gets the next rank.

Return the array of ranks, in the original order.

examples.why: Both 10s share rank 1. The 20 is rank 2, not 3: duplicates do not leave a gap.
The distinct values in order are -5, 0, 7. Negative numbers rank like any other value.

hints: The rank of a value only depends on how many distinct values are smaller than it.
Sort the distinct values once. The rank of a value is its position in that sorted list, plus one.
Store value → rank in a hash map while walking the sorted distinct values, then map the original array through it.

explain.intuition:
A value's rank is one more than the number of distinct values below it. Sorting the distinct values lines them up in exactly that order, so position p in the sorted list means rank p + 1.

A hash map from value to rank then turns the original array into ranks in one pass, keeping the original order. It is the same trick as turning a list of category names into stable numeric ids for a chart axis.
steps: Collect the distinct values (a Set) and sort them numerically.
Walk the sorted list and store value → index + 1 in a map.
pitfalls: Ranking by position in the sorted array with duplicates kept. [40, 10, 20, 10] would give 20 the rank 3 instead of 2.
Using JavaScript's default sort(), which compares numbers as text: 100 sorts before 20.
Returning ranks in sorted order instead of the original order.

solutions.title: Count smaller distinct values for each element
solutions.idea: For every element, count how many distinct values are strictly smaller and add 1.

solutions.title: Sort distinct values, then look up
solutions.idea: Sort the distinct values, map each to its 1-based position, and translate the array through the map.

followups: Use competition ranking instead (1, 1, 3 for two ties then a larger value). What changes?
Values arrive one at a time and you must report each new value's current rank. Which structure helps?
